patch.value: Recorded agent provenance is unreadable in practice: the only projection carrying it also carries every JSON Patch operation at 63.5x the compact cost, and no read surface can filter on harness, model, effort, or instance

Every provenance dimension the product detects is written into the immutable record and then cannot be read back except by paying for the entire mutation payload, and none of them can be filtered on. Measured 2026-07-29 against the 2,186-item repository tracker with 41,021 history entries.

What is written. A live entry carries author, author_source, agent_harness, agent_instance, and an agent_provenance object holding model and effort with per-dimension source. On this machine effort resolves to xhigh from the environment and the harness resolves to claude-code, so four of the five dimensions are genuinely populated at write time.

What can be read. The row-level read surfaces are activity, events, and history. Each has exactly two projections. The compact projection emits id, op, ts, author and message and drops every provenance field. The full projection emits the whole entry including the complete JSON Patch array. There is no third shape. So the only way to learn which harness, instance, model or effort produced a mutation is to also transport every patch operation of every mutation in the window.

The cost of that choice, measured. On the repository tracker, activity --compact --limit 50 is 10,568 bytes, roughly 2,642 tokens. The same window under --full is 671,002 bytes, roughly 167,750 tokens. That is 63.5 times more output to obtain five short scalars per row. A question as small as which harness closed the last fifty items therefore costs more than most context windows hold, and the answer would occupy a few hundred bytes.

What can be filtered. activity accepts --id, --op, --author, --from, --to. events accepts --since, --type, --author, --item. Neither accepts a harness, a model, an effort, an instance, or a session. The single identity filter is --author, and the mandated auto-detection collapses every process of a given harness to one literal value, so --author harness:claude-code selects the union of every Claude Code agent that ever ran, which is the same collapse that makes claim mutual exclusion unenforceable on pm-z8qd4k. Filtering by the dimension that actually distinguishes two concurrent agents, agent_instance, is impossible even though the value is recorded on every entry.

Coverage makes the read gap worse rather than better. Of 41,021 entries, 1,475 carry an agent_provenance object at all, effort is present on 224 of those, and model is null on 1,475 of 1,475. So the dimension that is most expensive to reach is also the one most often absent, and there is no way to ask the corpus how much provenance it actually has without reading all of it.

Why this is upstream of the analytics item. pm-gw6uyq specifies per-harness and per-model throughput, rework and defect-escape rates derived from immutable history alone, grouped by harness, model and author_source. Those aggregates cannot be computed by any consumer, including a package or an SDK caller, without a projection that yields provenance without patches and a predicate that selects on it. The analytics item is blocked on this primitive, not the other way round.

Scope boundary. This item is the read side only: a provenance projection on the row surfaces, and predicates over the recorded dimensions. Which dimensions exist and how they are detected stays with pm-rbg1qo for descriptor coverage and pm-ffz0a9 for the model resolver. What the aggregates mean stays with pm-gw6uyq. Whether a detected identity may be trusted for authorization stays out of all of them.

patch.value: A provenance projection exists on activity, events and history that emits author, author_source, agent_harness, agent_instance and every declared agent_provenance dimension without any JSON Patch payload, and its per-row cost stays within a small constant of the compact projection rather than a multiple of it; The row surfaces accept predicates on the recorded provenance dimensions, at minimum harness, model, effort and agent_instance, using the same filter grammar the existing --author and --op filters use, and an unknown dimension name fails fast naming the declared set rather than returning zero rows; Selecting one concurrent agent is possible: two processes of the same harness writing in the same window are separable by agent_instance through a documented filter, proven by a test that runs two writers and asserts each predicate returns only its own entries; A corpus-level coverage answer is cheap: a bounded summary reports how many entries carry each provenance dimension and how many do not, without transporting the entries, so an operator can measure provenance completeness before trusting any grouping; Dimensions added later flow through automatically: adding a declared dimension to the descriptor contract makes it projectable and filterable with no edit to activity, events, or history, proven by a fixture dimension that no built-in harness declares; The projection and the predicates are public SDK primitives first and the CLI flags are thin callers of them, so a package or an external consumer can build fleet analytics without reimplementing history parsing

value.text: Reproduced 2026-08-02 on the real tracker. 'pm history <id> --limit 1 --json' returns rows under compact_history whose complete key set is exactly [author, changed_fields, index, op, patch_ops, ts] - no harness, no model, no effort, no agent_instance, no session topic or role. The raw stream file carries all of them (agent_harness, agent_instance, agent_provenance.{model,effort,role,topic}), so the data exists and the only projection that renders it is the unbounded one. Confirms the item's framing from the read side: an agent that wants provenance must either parse .agents/pm/history/*.jsonl directly, which AGENTS.md forbids, or pay the full patch_ops payload.
